examples.title: Filtering Rows
examples.description: Keep only the rows that match a condition
examples.markdown:
## Filtering rows

`pl.col('Flavor') == 'chocolate'` is an expression: polars works it out for every row at once, giving a column of True and False. `filter` keeps the rows where it is True.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

# Only the chocolate cones
chocolate = cones.filter(pl.col('Flavor') == 'chocolate')
chocolate

examples.title: Two Conditions
examples.markdown:
## Two conditions at once

`&` means both must be True, `|` means either. Each condition needs its own parentheses.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

# Cones over $4 that are not chocolate
pricey = cones.filter((pl.col('Price') > 4) & (pl.col('Flavor') != 'chocolate'))
pricey

examples.title: Sorting Rows
examples.description: Put rows in order of a column
examples.markdown:
## Sorting

`sort` puts the rows in order of a column. polars has no index, so a row's position is its only label.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

# Most expensive first
by_price = cones.sort('Price', descending=True)
by_price

examples.title: Group and Average
examples.description: One row per group, with its mean
examples.markdown:
## Grouping

`group_by` gathers the rows with the same flavor; `agg` says what to work out for each group. `maintain_order=True` keeps the groups in the order they first appear.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

# Average price of each flavor
avg = cones.group_by('Flavor', maintain_order=True).agg(pl.col('Price').mean())
avg

examples.title: Counting Rows
examples.description: How many rows each group has
examples.markdown:
## Counting

`len()` counts the rows in each group.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

# How many cones of each flavor
counts = cones.group_by('Flavor', maintain_order=True).len()
counts

examples.title: Several Aggregations
examples.markdown:
## Several results per group

`agg` takes as many expressions as you like. `alias` names the column each one makes.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

# Cheapest and priciest cone of each flavor
range_ = cones.group_by('Flavor', maintain_order=True).agg(
    pl.col('Price').min().alias('cheapest'),
    pl.col('Price').max().alias('priciest'),
)
range_

examples.title: Adding a Column
examples.description: Work out a new column from others
examples.markdown:
## A new column

`with_columns` works an expression out for the whole column at once. `alias` names it.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

# A 10% sale
sale = cones.with_columns((pl.col('Price') * 0.9).alias('Sale'))
sale

examples.title: Selecting Columns
examples.markdown:
## Choosing columns

`select` makes a table from the columns and expressions you list, and nothing else.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

# Flavor and the price in cents
cents = cones.select('Flavor', (pl.col('Price') * 100).round(0).alias('Cents'))
cents

examples.title: Pivot
examples.markdown:
## Pivot

Each flavor becomes a row and each color a column; each cell is the mean price of the cones that fall into it.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

grid = cones.pivot(on='Color', index='Flavor', values='Price', aggregate_function='mean')
grid

examples.title: A Lazy Query
examples.description: Build a plan, then collect() it
examples.markdown:
## Lazy queries

`lazy()` makes a LazyFrame: each method adds to a plan and nothing runs yet. `collect()` optimizes the plan and runs it. The steps show the table after each part of the plan.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

summary = (
    cones.lazy()
    .filter(pl.col('Price') > 4)
    .group_by('Flavor', maintain_order=True)
    .agg(pl.col('Price').max())
    .sort('Price')
    .collect()
)
summary

examples.title: Chaining Operations
examples.description: Filter, add a column and sort in one expression
examples.markdown:
## A chain

Each method works on the result of the one before. Step through to see the table after each one.
cells: import polars as pl

# An ice cream shop's menu
cones = pl.DataFrame({
    'Flavor': ['strawberry', 'chocolate', 'vanilla', 'chocolate', 'strawberry', 'mint'],
    'Color': ['pink', 'light brown', 'white', 'dark brown', 'pink', 'green'],
    'Price': [3.55, 4.75, 4.25, 5.25, 3.95, 4.50],
})
cones

deals = (
    cones.filter(pl.col('Price') > 4)
    .with_columns((pl.col('Price') * 0.9).alias('Sale'))
    .sort('Sale')
)
deals
